param.label: Reference genome
param.help: The reference genome is required for generating a decoy-away index. The decoy sequences are regions of the target genome that are sequence similar to annotated transcripts. These are the regions of the genome most likely to cause mismapping.

param.label: Discard orphan quasi
param.help: Discard orphan mappings in quasi-mapping mode. If this flag is passed then only paired mappings will be considered toward quantification estimates. The default behavior is to consider orphan mappings if no valid paired mappings exist.

param.label: Min Score Fraction
param.help: The fraction of the optimal possible alignment score that a mapping must achieve in order to be considered valid. Should be in (0,1].

param.name: matchScore
param.label: Match Score
param.help: The value given to a match between read and reference nucleotides in an alignment.

param.name: mismatchPenalty
param.label: Mismatch Penalty
param.help: The value given to a mis-match between read and reference nucleotides in an alignment. This will be cast to a negative value.

param.name: gapOpenPenalty
param.label: Gap Open Penalty
param.help: The value given to a gap opening in an alignment.

param.name: gapExtensionPenalty
param.label: Gap Extension Penalty
param.help: The value given to a gap extension in an alignment.

param.label: Hard Filter
param.help: Instead of weighting mappings by their alignment score, this flag will discard any mappings with sub-optimal alignment score. The default option of soft-filtering (i.e. weighting mappings by their alignment score) usually yields slightly more accurate abundance estimates but this flag may be desirable if you want more accurate 'naive' equivalence classes, rather than range factorized equivalence classes.

param.label: Consensus Slack
param.help: The amount of slack allowed in the quasi-mapping consensus mechanism. Normally, a transcript must cover all hits to be considered for mapping. If this is set to a value, X, greater than 0, then a transcript can fail to cover up to X hits before it is discounted as a mapping candidate.

param.name: dovetail
param.label: Allow Dovetail
param.help: Allow dovetail mappings

param.label: Recover Orphans
param.help: Attempt to recover the mates of orphaned reads. This uses edlib for orphan recovery, and so introduces some computational overhead, but it can improve sensitivity.

param.label: Write Mappings to BAM File
param.help: If this option is provided, then the mapping results will be written out in SAM-compatible format. By default, output will be directed to stdout, but an alternative file name can be provided instead

param.name: afile
param.label: Alignment file
param.help: Salmon 2.x requires read-name-grouped (collated) alignments. The tool will collate a coordinate-sorted BAM for you; a name-sorted BAM is used as-is.

param.label: Discard orphans
param.help: Discard orphan alignments in the input. If this flag is passed, then only paired alignments will be considered toward quantification estimates. The default behavior is to consider orphan alignments if no valid paired mappings exist.

param.label: No Error Model
param.help: Turn off the alignment error model, which takes into account the the observed frequency of different types of mismatches / indels when computing the likelihood of a given alignment. Turning this off can speed up alignment-based salmon, but can harm quantification accuracy.

param.label: Number of Error Bins
param.help: The number of bins into which to divide each read when learning and applying the error model. For example, a value of 10 would mean that effectively, a separate error model is learned and applied to each 10th of the read, while a value of 3 would mean that a separate error model is applied to the read beginning (first third), middle (second third) and end (final third).

param.label: File containing a mapping of transcripts to genes
param.help: If this file is provided Salmon will output both quant.sf and quant.genes.sf files, where the latter contains aggregated gene-level abundance estimates. The transcript to gene mapping should be provided as either a GTF file, or a in a simple tab-delimited format where each line contains the name of a transcript and the gene to which it belongs separated by a tab.

param.label: Ignore transcript versions in the gene map
param.help: Ignore a trailing version suffix (for example '.1') on transcript names when matching them against the gene map. Enable this when combining an Ensembl cDNA FASTA (which carries versioned names) with an Ensembl GTF (which does not).

Sets the prior probability that an alignment that disagrees with the specified library type (orientation and strandedness) results from the true fragment origin. Setting this to 0 specifies that alignments that disagree with the library type should be 'impossible', while setting it to 1 says that alignments that disagree with the library type are no less likely than those that do

param.label: Meta
param.help: If you're using Salmon on a metagenomic dataset, consider setting this flag to disable parts of the abundance estimation model that make less sense for metagenomic data.

param.label: Use sketch (pseudoalignment) mode
param.help: New in salmon 2.x. Use pseudoalignment instead of selective alignment. This is generally faster and uses less memory, at some cost in accuracy for reads with many sequencing errors.

param.label: skipQuant
param.help: Skip performing the actual transcript quantification (including any Gibbs sampling or bootstrapping).

param.label: Dump equivalence class counts
param.help: Dump the equivalence class counts that were computed during quasi-mapping.

param.label: Dump equivalence class counts including rich weights
param.help: Includes 'rich' equivlance class weights in the output when equivalence class information is being dumped to file.

param.label: The value at which the fragment length PMF is down-sampled when evaluating GC fragment bias.
param.help: Larger values speed up effective length correction, but may decrease the fidelity of bias modeling results.

param.label: The maximum fragment length to consider when building the empirical distribution.
The mean used in the fragment length distribution prior
param.help: If single end reads are being used for quantification, or there are an insufficient number of uniquely mapping reads when performing paired-end quantification to estimate the empirical fragment length distribution, then use this value to calculate effective lengths.

param.label: Standard deviation
param.help: The standard deviation used in the fragment length distribution prior.

param.label: The forgetting factor used in the online learning schedule.
param.help: A smaller value results in quicker learning, but higher variance and may be unstable. A larger value results in slower learning but may be more stable. Value should be in the interval (0.5, 1.0].

param.label: Initialization with uniform parameters
param.help: initialize the offline inference with uniform parameters, rather than seeding with online parameters.

param.label: Maximal read mapping occurence
param.help: Reads mapping to more than this many places won't be considered.

param.label: No length correction
param.help: [experimental] : Entirely disables length correction when estimating the abundance of transcripts. This option can be used with protocols where one expects that fragments derive from their underlying targets without regard to that target's length (e.g. QuantSeq)

param.label: Disable effective length correction
param.help: Disables effective length correction when computing the probability that a fragment was generated from a transcript. If this flag is passed in, the fragment length distribution is not taken into account when computing this probability.

param.label: [experimental] : If this option is enabled, then no (lower) threshold will be set on how short bias correction can make effecctive lengths.
param.help: This can increase the precision of bias correction, but harm robustness. The default correction applies a threshold.

param.label: The first numAuxModelSamples are used to train the auxiliary model parameters.
param.help: (e.g. fragment length distribution, bias, etc.). After ther first numAuxModelSamples observations the auxiliary model parameters will be assumed to have converged and will be fixed.

param.label: Use the traditional EM algorithm for optimization in the batch passes.
Range of factorization bins
param.help: Factorizes the likelihood used in quantification by adopting a new notion of equivalence classes based on the conditional probabilities with which fragments are generated from different transcripts. This is a more fine-grained factorization than the normal rich equivalence classes. The default value (0) corresponds to the standard rich equivalence classes, and larger values imply a more fine-grained factorization. If range factorization is enabled, a common value to select for this parameter is 4.

param.label: Number of Gibbs sampling rounds to perform.
Number of bootstrap samples to generate. Note: This is mutually exclusive with Gibbs sampling.
Thinning factor
param.help: Number of steps to discard for every sample kept from the Gibbs chain. The larger this number, the less chance that subsequent samples are auto-correlated, but the slower sampling becomes.

param.label: The prior will be interpreted as a transcript-level prior.
param.help: either the default or the argument provided via --vbPrior

param.label: Significant Digits
param.help: The number of significant digits to write when outputting the EffectiveLength and NumReads columns.

param.label: The prior that will be used in the VBEM algorithm.
param.help: This is interpreted as a per-nucleotide prior, unless the --perTranscriptPrior flag is also given, in which case this is used as a transcript-level prior.

Salmon is a lightweight method for quantifying transcript abundance from RNA-seq reads, combining a dual-phase parallel inference algorithm and feature-rich bias models with an ultra-fast read mapping procedure.
The salmon package contains these tools:
* Index: creates a salmon index
* Quant: quantifies a sample (Reads or mapping-based)
* Quantmerge: Merges multiple quantifications into a single file
Galaxy divides these into separate tools in the toolshed:
* Salmon quant
* Salmon quantmerge
**Important note about salmon 2.x**
Salmon 2.0 is a from-scratch rewrite in Rust. It uses a **new index format**: indices built with the previous C++ salmon (up to 1.12.x) cannot be read and must be rebuilt with `salmon index`. The `salmon alevin` subcommand was removed; single-cell quantification has moved to the alevin-fry ecosystem (https://github.com/COMBINE-lab/alevin-fry). Long-read (Oxford Nanopore / PacBio) quantification is also no longer supported and is handled by oarfish (https://github.com/COMBINE-lab/oarfish).
